newsitem.title: USA: Attorney Roy Black to defend bond dealer Grigsby.
newsitem.headline: Attorney Roy Black to defend bond dealer Grigsby.

text.p: Defense attorney Roy Black said Friday he had been hired by California bond dealer Calvin Grigsby in relation to a federal grand jury investigation involving Dade County, Fla., bonds.

In a brief conversation with Reuters, Black confirmed that he had been in touch with federal officials conducting the investigation and that the grand jury probe did involve allegations of corruption in Dade County bond deals.
He said there was no indication when or if or what charges might be filed.
"They haven't said anything at all about the charges," Black said. "All they said is there's an investigation and I could talk to them."

Dade County officials said late last year they were subpoenaed before the grand jury to testify about Dade bond deals underwritten by Grigsby's San Francisco firm, which was then called Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc.

The Miami Herald reported that the FBI had videotaped a conversation in which Grigsby offered Dade County Commissioner James Burke a kickback in exchange for Burke's steering bond work his way. Neither the FBI nor other federal investigators would comment on that report, and Grigsby and Burke have both said they are innocent of wrongdoing.
Asked if Grigsby would consider any sort of plea agreement with the federal government, Black said, "He said he's innocent."
Black said he did not know who else may be a target of the grand jury investigation.
"We're really not aware of the scope of their investigation," he said.
